title: Technology Sector Update for 06/18/2018: MU,MNLX,GOOG,GOOGL,JD,IRM

Technology stocks were edging higher in late Monday trade, reversing prior declines, with shares of tech companies in the S&P 500 adding almost 0.2% in value today although the Philadelphia semiconductor index was posting a more than 0.9% decline.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
+ Micron Technology ( MU ) was hanging on to a small gain Monday afternoon, recovering from declines earlier in the session, after Barclays analyst Blayne Curtis said Memory pricing has held together better than expected recently, boosting the revenue and earnings outlooks for memory chipmakers like Micron Tech. DRAM spot pricing has ticked down, Curtis observed, but is still above contract, which has gained 3% in the past three months due to "robust" demand from cloud data centers. "On the flash side, we acknowledge incremental capacity is coming online and there is a risk server demand moderates more than handsets offset, but for now contract remains stable and the fall in pricing has opened new demand pipelines (particularly in SSDs)," he said.
In other sector news:
+ Alphabet ( GOOG ) was more than 1% higher after the technology conglomerate said it was investing $550 million in JD.Com ( JD ) as part of new strategic partnership "to enable helpful, personalized and frictionless shopping experiences in several regions including Southeast Asia, the U.S. and Europe." Alphabet will receive 27.1 million newly issued JD.com shares at $20.29 apiece, equivalent to $40.58 per American Depositary Share, based on the volume-weighted average trading price over the past 10 days.
- Iron Mountain ( IRM ) fell Monday after saying it purchase Croatia-based Arhiv Trezor, a provider of records management, destruction and transportation services, for an undisclosed amount. The acquisition introduces Iron Mountain into southeastern Europe.
- Mellanox Technologies ( MLNX ) was more than 2% lower in recent Monday trading, staying with close range of its session low, despite reports the fabless chipmaker was near a settlement with activist investors Starboard Value over its board composition. Under the proposed agreement, Mellanox will add two members from Starboard's eight-person nominee slate to its board of directors, according to a Reuters report, citing unnamed sources familiar with the matter. The report did not identify the Starboard candidates who will join the 11-member panel and also did not say which current directors will step down although it said Mellanox board chairman Irwin Federman will remain in his post and the sources also said that Starboard portfolio manager Peter Feld will not receive a board seat. In exchange for the two board seats, Starboard accepted a standstill agreement and will support the board make-up for at least one year. The sources cautioned that the agreement was preliminary and that final terms of the pact could change.
